result.summary: This PR expands the doxygen-style comments in net.h to spell out the call-order contract for NetEventsInterface's InitializeNode/ProcessMessages/SendMessages/FinalizeNode methods, and documents how CConnman safely destroys CNode objects via reference counting and the m_nodes/m_nodes_disconnected lists. It is a documentation-only change with no functional code modifications. The commit is co-authored with ajtowns, reflecting incorporated review suggestions.
result.problem: The lifetime and threading rules around CNode destruction and the NetEventsInterface callback contract were previously undocumented or only implicitly understood, making it easy for future contributors modifying net.cpp to introduce use-after-free or ordering bugs.

result.card: This PR (net.h only, +61/-6) adds detailed documentation of the NetEventsInterface method call order and the CNode reference-counted destruction sequence in CConnman, with no functional code change. It solves a real but low-severity problem: future contributors modifying net.cpp lack a clear written contract for safe CNode lifetime management, risking use-after-free bugs if misunderstood. The strongest evidence of value is ajtowns' detailed, adopted review feedback rewriting the destruction-sequence documentation and requesting further clarification on concurrent-access safety, all incorporated by the author (now co-author). Review is technically ready since all raised points were addressed, but the author has been silent for 86 days since the last rebase, and a maintainer recently suggested the PR may no longer interest reviewers. No dependencies block this PR, and it does not itself unblock other named work beyond making future net.cpp changes safer to write and review.
